featured_reviews.name: Utkarsh Dalal
featured_reviews.review_text:
First things first, the staff both at the building and at the coworking space were polite and lovely. However, that is the only positive thing I have to say. This may be the worst coworking space I have ever been to, and I'm genuinely shocked that they even market it as a coworking space.

What it is is a glorified cafe - if you get a day pass and try to work here, they shove you into a random table in the corner of their lunch room (picture attached), with uncomfortable and unergonomic chairs. My shoulder started hurting within a few minutes of sitting here.

Since it is their lunch room, it's also not quiet - so not suitable for working, and definitely not suitable for taking calls or meetings. There is no room for taking calls.

There is coffee and water, but you have to take it in a tiny paper cup (photo attached). I don't think they even had crockery or cutlery to eat lunch with.

To make matters worse, the address they send of the location on Google Maps is wrong (wrong side of the street), and getting to the space is an absolute maze and none of this is explained beforehand. You have to hand full a register on the ground floor, take a lift up one floor, walk out and past a Starbucks, then go through another gate, where you will find lifts of which only one of them actually goes to the 25th floor. It took me 20 minutes to go from the entrance of the building to the entrance of the space.

The bathroom is fine, and I guess there's a view if you're into that - but it was a hazy day.

I left in an hour and went home, which for myself and most people will be significantly quieter, more productive and more comfortable. I can't believe I paid money to work here and was in half a mind to ask for a refund.

featured_reviews.name: Chintani Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Summary: No space for discussion, no space for silence!

They have no space to take calls except for 3 uncomfortable phone booths. These do not fulfill the requirement of such a large office, so people have no option but to take calls elsewhere - which is not permitted!

There is no space except the pantry for a team to have short discussions. I understand the need to book a meeting room for a formal meeting, but how does a team function without any conversation all day?

Worst of all, they advertise 'Silent Zone' on their website. However, people have full-fledged, loud discussions and calls in these zones. When we inform the staff, we are told to mention specific cabin numbers, write e-mails, etc. Is it our responsibility to report others throughout the day?

They have a lovely deck overlooking the ocean, but they restrict entry to it! Instead of creating a progressive system to monitor authorized entry to the workspace, they decide to add restrictions at every stage, which makes the work experience rather unpleasant.

The location gives this the potential to become the best co-working space in the city. If they would simply demarcate one Silent Zone for people who actually need silence and open other spaces for in-team discussions, collaboration would become very simple indeed.

P.S. - I guess those who have booked full cabins for their company have a slightly better experience in terms of calls/silence, but I don't think others should be treated as second-class citizens or lured with the promise of a Silent Zone, which is anything but one!

P.P.S. - Also, they have really bad coffee and tea!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Hi Chintani, we apologise for the unpleasant experience. We will surely communicate your feedback to the concerned team. You can also share your feedback in detail along with your contact details at we-in-48093@wework.co.in so that the concerned team can get in touch with you.
